Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; can you describe exactly when these symptoms started and how severe they are?

REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulse_Oximetry: 88% on room air, improving with oxygen. Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, PaO2 60 mm Hg, HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood gas indicates respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia; does the baby have any cyanosis, grunting, or nasal flaring, and was the birth normal or complicated?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical presentation of respiratory acidosis, hypoxemia, and the chest X-ray findings of ground-glass opacity with air bronchograms are classic for RDS due to surfactant deficiency.
